title: Attention Is All You Need
text: The Transformer uses attention instead of recurrent or convolutional layers for sequence transduction. Its encoder and decoder were evaluated on machine translation. Removing recurrence allows more parallel computation during training. The paper reports translation results on English to German and English to French, and also explores constituency parsing. This note does not specify deployment costs for modern hardware.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
text: BERT learns language representations using context on both sides of a token throughout its layers. A pretrained model can be adapted to question answering and language inference with an additional output layer. The work evaluates eleven natural language processing tasks. Bidirectional contextual representations are its central distinction from approaches that restrict pretraining to a single direction.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
text: DPR retrieves passages using learned dense vectors rather than only lexical matching. A dual encoder learns representations from question and passage examples. The paper compares passage retrieval against a Lucene BM25 baseline across open domain question answering datasets. Better retrieval supplies relevant contexts to a downstream answering system. The reported gains belong to those experiments and do not establish performance on this research-note corpus.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
text: RAG combines a pretrained sequence to sequence generator with an external dense index of Wikipedia passages. A neural retriever provides nonparametric memory alongside knowledge stored in model parameters. One formulation uses the same retrieved passages for an entire generated sequence; another can change passages for each generated token. The work evaluates knowledge intensive NLP tasks, including open domain question answering.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
text: ColBERT independently encodes queries and documents with BERT, then applies a late interaction step for fine grained matching. Document representations can be computed before queries arrive. This architecture aims to retain expressive matching while reducing the cost of jointly processing every query document pair. The paper studies both reranking and retrieval using vector similarity indexes.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
text: LoRA keeps pretrained model weights frozen and trains low rank decomposition matrices to adapt a Transformer. Updating fewer parameters reduces the training memory and storage needed for task specific models compared with full fine tuning. The paper studies several language model families and discusses rank deficiency in adaptation. LoRA itself does not require quantizing the frozen weights.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
text: DPO adapts a language model to preference comparisons with a classification objective derived from a reward parameterization. It simplifies the usual reinforcement learning from human feedback procedure, avoiding an explicit separate reward fitting and reinforcement learning optimization pipeline. The paper evaluates sentiment control, summarization and dialogue. This approach addresses preference alignment rather than passage retrieval.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
text: QLoRA combines frozen four bit quantized model weights with trainable low rank adapters. Gradients pass through the frozen model into the adapters. Its memory saving techniques include NormalFloat 4, double quantization of quantization constants and paged optimizers for memory spikes. The paper reports adapting a 65 billion parameter model on one 48 GB GPU. This experimental setting is not a guarantee for arbitrary models or workloads.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
text: Sentence BERT uses siamese and triplet training structures to produce sentence embeddings that can be compared with cosine similarity. Computing representations independently avoids repeatedly running BERT on every possible sentence pair. The work targets efficient semantic similarity search and evaluates semantic textual similarity and transfer tasks. It distinguishes embedding based comparison from jointly encoding each pair.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
text: InstructGPT first fine tunes a language model on human demonstrations of desired behavior. Human rankings of model outputs then support reinforcement learning from human feedback. The goal is better instruction following and alignment with user intent. Human evaluation favors the resulting model over a much larger unaligned baseline in the studied prompt distribution. The paper also examines truthfulness and toxic output generation.
